frontiers.name: Sub-GeV recoils
frontiers.known: Electronic, phonon and molecular excitations can lower thresholds.
frontiers.unknown: Background populations and signal yields at the few-quanta limit.
frontiers.decisive: Repeatable target-scaled spectrum with calibrated response.
frontiers.instrument: Cryogenic semiconductors, superconducting sensors, molecular and low-threshold ionisation targets.
frontiers.risk: Few-quanta backgrounds, quenching, detector response and surface events can imitate low-energy signals.

frontiers.name: Directional detection
frontiers.known: A Galactic-wind direction differs from most terrestrial backgrounds.
frontiers.unknown: Whether scalable targets retain recoil direction at low energy.
frontiers.decisive: Sidereal directional modulation reproduced in independent targets.
frontiers.instrument: Low-pressure TPCs, anisotropic crystals and directional solid-state targets with sidereal timing.
frontiers.risk: Direction information can be erased by diffusion, thresholds and reconstruction bias before reaching the analysis.

frontiers.name: Axion and wave sensing
frontiers.known: Coherent fields can convert or drive resonant responses.
frontiers.unknown: The relevant mass/frequency and coupling, if any.
frontiers.decisive: Frequency-coherent signal that tracks magnetic field or apparatus configuration.
frontiers.instrument: Microwave cavities, lumped-element resonators, dielectric haloscopes, magnets and quantum sensors.
frontiers.risk: Environmental lines and apparatus resonances can mimic narrow coherent signals unless field/configuration scaling is reproduced.

frontiers.name: Precision timing
frontiers.known: Clocks, pulsars and interferometers test transient or oscillatory fields.
frontiers.unknown: Noise correlations and realistic dark-structure encounter rates.
frontiers.decisive: Correlated propagation pattern across separated instruments.
frontiers.instrument: Optical clocks, pulsar timing arrays, atom interferometers and geographically separated precision networks.
frontiers.risk: Clock noise, ephemeris errors and correlated environmental disturbances can masquerade as a coherent field.

frontiers.name: Survey-scale lensing
frontiers.known: Gravity coherently distorts many background sources.
frontiers.unknown: Baryonic feedback, redshift and shear-calibration degeneracies.
frontiers.decisive: Consistent mass maps across surveys, wavelengths and pipelines.
frontiers.instrument: Rubin, Euclid, Roman, CMB lensing and multi-band shear/redshift calibration.
frontiers.risk: Photometric-redshift bias, PSF/shear calibration and baryonic feedback can shift reconstructed mass maps.

frontiers.name: Small-scale structure
frontiers.known: Free streaming, waves and self-interactions alter halo populations.
frontiers.unknown: How baryonic physics mimics or erases those signatures.
frontiers.decisive: One microphysical model matching satellites, streams, lenses and clusters.
frontiers.instrument: Strong-lens substructure, stellar streams, satellite populations and high-resolution simulations.
frontiers.risk: Baryonic feedback and selection effects can mimic or erase the signatures attributed to dark microphysics.

timeline.capability: Cross-calibrated surveys, multi-tonne rare-event searches, axion scans and precision timing
timeline.gate: Blind analyses, calibrated backgrounds, public data products and independent pipelines

timeline.capability: Lower thresholds, larger directional prototypes, denser lensing maps and stronger multi-survey cross-calibration
timeline.gate: Any candidate signal must scale with target, time, direction, field setting or instrument as predicted

timeline.capability: Background-limited observatories, mature directional detectors and networked quantum sensors if viable parameter space motivates them
timeline.gate: Independent replication or decisive retirement of major candidate regions

timeline.capability: Facilities optimised around whatever microscopic or gravitational parameter space survives
timeline.gate: A common physical model must jointly explain laboratory, Galactic and cosmological observables before engineering claims are promoted

timeline.capability: Direct dark-sector metrology, communication or controlled production only if a reproducible controllable coupling has been discovered
timeline.gate: Demonstrated generation/detection with an explicit link budget and conservation-law accounting

timeline.capability: Energy extraction, propulsion or material-like dark-sector engineering only if capture, confinement and usable energy/momentum transfer are demonstrated
timeline.gate: Laboratory control must precede system engineering; current evidence provides no such mechanism

timeline.capability: Reactionless drives, gravity shielding, faster-than-light travel or dimensional shortcuts
timeline.gate: No route follows from current dark-matter evidence; requires independently established new physics

timeline_contract: Horizons are planning frames, not discovery forecasts. Capabilities advance only when the stated validation gate is satisfied.

technology_gates.label: Identity
technology_gates.requirement: Microscopic state or field identified with reproducible observables.

technology_gates.label: Coupling
technology_gates.requirement: Interaction with ordinary matter or another controllable sector measured.

technology_gates.label: Control
technology_gates.requirement: Interaction strength/state can be deliberately prepared or modulated.

technology_gates.label: Capture or confinement
technology_gates.requirement: A demonstrable way to retain or repeatedly interact with the dark state exists.

technology_gates.label: Energy transfer
technology_gates.requirement: Usable energy transfer exceeds backgrounds and system overheads.

technology_gates.label: Directed momentum
technology_gates.requirement: Momentum exchange can be directed while conserving total momentum.

technology_gates.label: Engineering
technology_gates.requirement: A complete mass, power, heat, shielding, reliability and trajectory budget closes.
